MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.description: Modifier stacking uses TWO separate pools that never cross-apply. Prep tasks use condition_scale x component_modifier (baluster_profile OR stringer_type+access). Coating tasks use quality_tier x component_modifier. Contamination drives task ACTIVATION, not rate modification.
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_prep: POOR(2.00) x open_stringer(1.40) x scaffolding(2.00) = 5.60x — extremely rare residential RP, flag for estimator review
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.worst_case_coating: QT5(1.50) x open_stringer(1.40) x scaffolding(2.00) = 4.20x — extremely rare residential, flag for review
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.realistic_max_prep: POOR(2.00) x turned_baluster(1.75) = 3.50x for baluster prep; POOR(2.00) x open_stringer(1.40) x step_ladder(1.30) = 3.64x for stringer prep
MODIFIER_STACKING_WARNING.realistic_max_coating: QT5(1.50) x turned_baluster(1.75) = 2.63x for baluster coating; QT5(1.50) x open_stringer(1.40) x step_ladder(1.30) = 2.73x for stringer coating

prep_tasks.component_modifiers: FAC_BALUSTER_PROFILE (baluster tasks) OR FAC_STRINGER_TYPE + FAC_STAIRWELL_ACCESS (stringer tasks) OR 1.0x (riser/newel/handrail/base_rail)

coating_tasks.component_modifiers: FAC_BALUSTER_PROFILE (baluster tasks) OR FAC_STRINGER_TYPE + FAC_STAIRWELL_ACCESS (stringer tasks) OR 1.0x (riser/newel/handrail/base_rail)

task_production_rates.name: Install Tread Protection (Ram Board Stair Armor)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_TREAD_PROTECT (25 EA/hr). ~2.5 min per tread for Ram Board Stair Armor install. Includes positioning, securing with Safe-Release tape. Standard flight of 14 treads = ~35 min. FIRST task — mandatory at all tiers.

task_production_rates.name: Install Landing Floor Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_FLOOR_PROTECT (200 SF/hr). Canvas drop cloth layout at landings. Standard protection rate. In RP, landing floors are almost always finished.

task_production_rates.name: Mask Walls Along Stringer Edge and Railing Area
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_WALL_MASK / TSK_STRL_WALL_MASK (both 120 LF/hr). Tape and paper along stringer top edge and railing wall area. Standard masking rate.

task_production_rates.name: Set Up Baluster Spray Containment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_CONTAIN (45 min FIXED). Per system. Cardboard shields behind balusters, junction taping. Time varies with baluster count — 45 min is typical for 39-62 baluster system.

task_production_rates.name: Protect Carpet Runner
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Rosin paper over carpet edges where paint work occurs. Low-tack Safe-Release tape to avoid carpet backing damage. ~20 min per stairway system — similar to floor runner protection. Not present in NC.

task_production_rates.name: Install Wet Paint Safety Signage
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Install signs at top and bottom of stairway. ~5 min per system. Quick task but critical for occupied home safety.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Handrail Brackets (Label and Bag)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRACKET_REMOVE (12 EA/hr). ~5 min per bracket. Remove screws, label bracket, bag hardware, mark location on wall. QT4+ only. Typical: 3-5 brackets per handrail run. In RP, may encounter paint build-up on screw heads — captured in existing rate range.

task_production_rates.name: Visual Condition Inspection — All Stair Components
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Scan all 6 stair component types with work light: risers, stringers, balusters, newels, handrails, base rails. Map cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, wear patterns, staining. Assign condition_scale per component. More components than door RP assessment (~7-8 min/opening QT3). QT3: 8 min standard visual. QT4: 12 min systematic with raking light + photographs. QT5: 18 min critical assessment, multiple passes. Calibrated against door RP TSK_DIRP_ASSESS_CONDITION — stairs have more component types but assessed as a single system.

task_production_rates.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Cross-hatch tape test at minimum 4 locations (1 riser + 1 stringer + 1 baluster + 1 handrail). ~5 min per stairway system. Faster than door RP per-opening test because tests are concentrated in one area. Calibrated against door RP TSK_DIRP_ASSESS_ADHESION (~7-8 min per opening with 2 locations).

task_production_rates.name: Coating Identification — Latex vs Oil
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Solvent rub test at minimum 2 locations (riser + handrail). ~4 min per system. Critical for stairs — historically oil-based. Faster per-system than door RP per-opening test. Calibrated against door RP TSK_DIRP_ASSESS_COATING_ID (~5 min per opening).

task_production_rates.name: Anti-Slip Verification — Tread Protection Adequacy
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Verify tread protection is non-slip and secured. Check all treads — quick visual + tactile check. ~3 min per system. Safety assessment for occupied homes. No NC equivalent.

task_production_rates.name: Lead Test (XRF or Swab)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. Test at 4 locations minimum (1 riser + 1 stringer + 1 handrail + 1 baluster). ~15 min per stairway system. Stairs are HIGH RISK for lead paint — historically oil-based, multi-layer from multiple repaints. Stair-specific rate slightly longer than door RP (10 min) due to 4 test locations vs 2.

task_production_rates.name: RRP Containment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. Install poly sheeting containment at stairwell access points (top and bottom). Warning signs. ~30 min per system. Stairwell containment is more complex than room containment due to open vertical shaft — longer than door RP (15 min/opening). Per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

task_production_rates.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance. On stairs, dust settles on treads below — vacuum treads and landings. ~20 min per cycle. More surface area than single door opening.

task_production_rates.name: RRP Containment Removal and Visual Clearance
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. Remove containment poly from stairwell access points, visual clearance inspection. ~20 min per system. Slightly longer than door RP (10 min) due to vertical shaft containment complexity.

task_production_rates.name: Lead-Contaminated Waste Disposal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shared RRP module task. Package and dispose lead-contaminated debris per EPA RRP Rule. Fixed time per project. ~30 min. Consistent with door RP rate.

task_production_rates.name: TSP Wash All Stair Component Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. TSP wash of all stair component surfaces. Wipe-on, scrub detail areas (baluster junctions, newel caps), rinse, dry. ~30 min per stairway system. Stairs have extensive detail surface requiring scrubbing — longer than wall RP TSP wash (~20 min/room) due to multi-component geometry.

task_production_rates.name: Mildew/Biocide Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Bleach/mildewcide solution to affected areas. Full contact/kill time + rinse. ~20 min per system. Rare on stairs but possible in basement stairwells. Calibrated against door RP TSK_DIRP_TREAT_MILDEW (~15 min per opening). Stairs need more solution coverage if mildew is present.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Stringer Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical or mechanical degloss, all accessible stringer surfaces. ~1.2 min/LF.

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification on open stringer profiles. ~1.5 min/LF.

QT5.notes: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test. ~2 min/LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_STRS_SAND_PREP_STRINGER. NC sand prep was 60-100 LF/hr substrate-driven. RP degloss is slower: chemical degloss requires wipe-on, dwell, wipe-off vs simple scuff. Stringer profile is linear — faster per LF than door frame degloss per EA. QT3 baseline: ~50 LF/hr chemical degloss. Open stringer modifier: 1.4x (notched profile). Access modifier applies to stringer tasks only.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Riser Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical or mechanical degloss, full riser face. ~2 min/EA.

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification. ~2.5 min/EA.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_STRS_SAND_PREP_RISER. NC sand prep was 20-30 EA/hr substrate-driven. RP degloss: ~30 EA/hr QT3. Risers are flat vertical surfaces (~2.2 SF each) — efficient to degloss with sanding sponge. Per research A-003: degloss rates from trim/door RP patterns.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Baluster Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical preferred for turned profiles. ~3 min/EA (square baseline).

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification at junctions. ~4 min/EA.

QT5.notes: Complete degloss with verification, all profile surfaces. ~5 min/EA.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_BALUSTER + TSK_STRL_SCUFF_SAND_IRON. NC bare wood sand was 12 EA/hr square, 8 EA/hr turned. RP degloss of existing paint is faster than NC bare-wood full sand on flat profiles, but chemical degloss on turned profiles adds dwell time. Baluster_profile modifier: square=1.0x, turned=1.75x per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2. Per research A-003: ~12-20 EA/hr depending on profile.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Newel Post Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical degloss, all accessible surfaces. ~7.5 min/EA.

QT4.notes: Full degloss including caps, rosettes, detail areas. ~10 min/EA.

QT5.notes: Complete degloss with verification, all decorative detail. ~12 min/EA.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_NEWEL. NC bare sand was 5-8 EA/hr. RP degloss is comparable — newels have large surface area with decorative detail (caps, rosettes, flutes). Chemical degloss preferred for detail areas. QT3 baseline: ~8 EA/hr.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Handrail Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical or mechanical degloss, all 4 surfaces. ~1.5 min/LF.

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification, underside addressed. ~2 min/LF.

QT5.notes: Complete degloss all surfaces with verification. ~2.4 min/LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_HANDRAIL. NC bare sand was 40-60 LF/hr. RP degloss of handrails: 4 surfaces to degloss — chemical deglosser is efficient but requires dwell time. High wear on handrails means existing finish is often already dulled. QT3 baseline: ~40 LF/hr.

task_production_rates.name: Degloss Base Rail Surfaces

QT3.notes: Chemical or mechanical degloss, 3 accessible surfaces. ~1.2 min/LF.

QT4.notes: Full degloss with adhesion verification. ~1.5 min/LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW — replaces NC TSK_STRL_SAND_PREP_BASE_RAIL. NC bare sand was 50-75 LF/hr. RP degloss base rail: 3 surfaces vs handrail 4 surfaces — slightly faster. Conditional: not all systems have base rails. QT3 baseline: ~50 LF/hr.

task_production_rates.name: Scrape Loose Paint and Feather Edges — Risers and Stringers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Scrape failing paint from riser faces and stringer surfaces, feather-sand all edges. FIXED time per stairway system. QT3: 30 min baseline (spot scrape visible failures). QT4: 45 min (comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering). QT5: 60 min (critical scrape + perfect feathering). Stringer_type and access modifiers apply. Per research A-004: flat surfaces ~10-15 EA/hr risers equivalent. Combined riser+stringer as FIXED since they are worked together sequentially.

task_production_rates.name: Scrape Loose Paint and Feather Edges — Balusters, Newels, Handrails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Extremely labor-intensive for turned balusters — each baluster is a separate scrape/feather operation on complex profiles. Handrails have 4-surface access. FIXED time per system. QT3: 45 min baseline. QT4: 60 min comprehensive. QT5: 90 min critical. Baluster_profile modifier applies — turned profiles at 1.75x can push QT5 to 157 min. Per research A-004: profiled surfaces ~5-8 EA/hr balusters.

task_production_rates.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk — Stringer-to-Wall Junction

QT3.notes: Replace visibly failed sections — cracked or separated joints. ~0.75 min/LF.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints. ~1 min/LF.

QT5.notes: Critical assessment, replace all joints not in perfect condition. ~1.3 min/LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_CAULK_STRINGER_WALL (60 LF/hr full caulk). RP assess-and-replace is faster per LF than NC full caulk for GOOD condition (most joints intact, 15-30% replacement). QT3 baseline: 80 LF/hr. Closed stringers only — this is the stringer-to-wall junction. Higher tiers do more comprehensive assessment.

task_production_rates.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk — Riser-to-Stringer Junctions

QT3.notes: Replace visibly failed joints. ~3 min/EA for 2 joints.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive assessment of all riser-stringer joints. ~4 min/EA.

QT5.notes: Critical assessment, all joints in perfect condition. ~5 min/EA.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRS_CAULK_RISER_STRINGER (15 EA/hr full caulk, both joints). RP assess-and-replace: QT3 is faster than NC full caulk (~20 EA/hr) because only failed sections replaced (15-30% typical). 2 joints per riser at left/right stringer edges.

task_production_rates.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk — Newel Junction Joints

QT3.notes: Replace visibly failed newel junctions. ~6 min/EA.

QT4.notes: Comprehensive assessment of all newel junctions. ~7.5 min/EA.

QT5.notes: Critical assessment, all joints in perfect condition. ~10 min/EA.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: MODIFIED from NC TSK_STRL_CAULK_NEWEL (8 EA/hr full caulk). RP assess-and-replace for GOOD condition is faster (~10 EA/hr QT3) because only failed sections replaced. Newels have 2-3 joints each (newel-to-tread, newel-to-handrail). Higher tiers require more thorough assessment.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Sanding/Scraping Dust (Tack Cloth / Vacuum)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_CLEAN_DUST (15 min) + TSK_STRL_CLEAN_DUST (20 min). Combined RP spec cleans all components in single pass — not additive. ~25 min per system. Tack cloth all surfaces, vacuum treads and landings. HEPA vacuum recommended in RP occupied context.

task_production_rates.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Stringers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_PRIME_STRINGER (80 LF/hr brush prime). Comparable to baseboard brush rate. Primer type is state-driven (adhesion, stain-block, or mildew-resistant) but application rate is the same regardless of primer product. Open stringer modifier: 1.4x. Access modifier for stringer tasks.

task_production_rates.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Risers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_PRIME_RISER (15 EA/hr brush prime). ~4 min per riser (~2.2 SF each). Vertical surface — thin coat, no runs. State-driven primer selection but same application rate.

task_production_rates.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Balusters
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_PRIME_BALUSTER. Square: 15 EA/hr (~4 min/EA). Turned: 8.5 EA/hr (~7 min/EA). Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2. State-driven primer but same application rates. German round trim brush for turned profiles.

task_production_rates.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Newel Posts
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_PRIME_NEWEL (4 EA/hr). ~15 min/newel brush prime. Larger surface, more detail than balusters. Caps, rosettes, flutes require careful coverage.

task_production_rates.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Handrails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_PRIME_HANDRAIL (65 LF/hr brush prime). ~25% slower than flat trim (80 LF/hr) due to 4-surface access. QT4+: painting horizontally (brackets removed) is faster but rate accounts for average.

task_production_rates.name: Apply State-Driven Primer on Base Rails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_PRIME_BASE_RAIL (70 LF/hr). Slightly faster than handrail (3 surfaces vs 4). Conditional.

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Primer for Finish Coat Adhesion
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_SAND_PRIMER (20 min) + TSK_STRL_SAND_PRIMER (25 min). Combined RP spec sands all primed components in single pass — not fully additive. ~30 min per system. 220 grit light sand all primed surfaces. Tack cloth after.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Prime Scraped/Repaired Areas
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Spot prime all scraped areas, feathered edges, caulk replacements, patched areas. Brush application regardless of method. GOOD condition has fewer spots. QT3: 10 min (few spot areas). QT4: 15 min (more thorough). QT5: 20 min (all repairs with wide feather). Calibrated against door RP spot prime patterns.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Work Area Between Coats
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_CLEAN_AREA (10 min) + TSK_STRL_CLEAN_AREA (10 min). Combined RP spec cleans entire stairway in single pass. ~15 min per interstage cycle. Not fully additive — overlap in tread/landing cleaning.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Previous Coat — All Components
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_INSPECT_COAT (10/20/30 min) + TSK_STRL_INSPECT_COAT (15/25/40 min). Combined RP spec inspects all components in single pass. Not fully additive — some overlap. QT3: 15 min quick scan. QT4: 30 min systematic all components + junctions. QT5: 45 min critical with light, junction nibs, handrail underside.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Between Coats — All Components
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_SAND_BETWEEN (10/25/35 min) + TSK_STRL_SAND_BETWEEN (15/35/50 min). Combined RP spec sands all components in single pass. Not fully additive — some overlap in setup. QT3: 20 min spot sand nibs only. QT4: 45 min full 220 grit all surfaces. QT5: 60 min thorough 220-320 grit. Rigid sanding block for flat surfaces, contour sanding for turned profiles.

task_production_rates.name: Patch and Repair Marked Defects (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_PATCH_DEFECTS (5/15/25 min) + TSK_STRL_PATCH_DEFECTS (5/15/25 min). Combined: QT3: 8 min (combined defects from all components). QT4: 20 min. QT5: 35 min. Not fully additive — setup and tooling overlap.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_SPOT_COAT (5/10/15 min) + TSK_STRL_SPOT_COAT (5/10/15 min). Combined: QT3: 8 min. QT4: 15 min. QT5: 20 min. Touch-up patched areas before next full coat.

task_production_rates.name: Tack Cloth All Surfaces
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TACK_CLEAN (10 min) + TSK_STRL_TACK_CLEAN (15 min). Combined RP spec tack cleans all components in single pass. ~20 min per interstage cycle. Not fully additive.

task_production_rates.name: Verify Tread Protection Integrity (Daily)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Daily check + per interstage cycle. Quick visual + tactile verify of tread protection integrity. Repair/replace damaged sections. ~5 min per cycle. Critical safety task for occupied homes. NC had TSK_STRL_TREAD_PROTECT_VERIFY but as verification of existing install (40 EA/hr). RP uses fixed time per system check.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Stringers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_BRUSH_FINISH_STRINGER (85 LF/hr). Comparable to baseboard trim rates (80-90 LF/hr). Application quality is NOT tiered — same speed at all QTs. Open stringer modifier: 1.4x. Access modifier for stringer tasks.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Risers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_BRUSH_FINISH_RISER (15 EA/hr). ~4 min per riser. Vertical surface — apply, tip once, walk away. Check for sags before moving to next riser.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Balusters
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_BALUSTER. Square: 15 EA/hr (~4 min/EA). Turned: 8.5 EA/hr (~7 min/EA). Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2. German round trim brush + flow additive for turned profiles to prevent roping. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Newel Posts
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_NEWEL (4 EA/hr). ~15 min/newel per coat. Larger and more detailed than balusters. Caps, rosettes, flutes, all 4 sides.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Handrails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_HANDRAIL (65 LF/hr). 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). ~25% slower than flat trim (85 LF/hr). QT4+: painting horizontally (brackets removed) may be slightly faster.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat on Base Rails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRUSH_FINISH_BASE_RAIL (70 LF/hr). 3 surfaces — slightly faster than handrail. Conditional.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Stringers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_SPRAY_FINISH_STRINGER (350 LF/hr). Significantly faster than brush. Open stringer modifier: 1.4x. Requires wall masking.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Risers
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_SPRAY_FINISH_RISER (60 EA/hr). ~1 min per riser. Light passes on vertical surface.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Balusters
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_BALUSTER (40 EA/hr). ~2.5x faster than brush for square. HVLP preferred. All profiles spray at similar rates (profile complexity affects brush, not spray). Containment must be in place.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Newel Posts
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_NEWEL (12 EA/hr). ~3x faster than brush (4 EA/hr). Larger target, easy to spray.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Handrails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_HANDRAIL (200 LF/hr). ~3x faster than brush. Light passes on all 4 surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat on Base Rails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_SPRAY_FINISH_BASE_RAIL (220 LF/hr). Slightly faster than handrail (3 surfaces). Conditional.

task_production_rates.name: Final Quality Inspection — All Components
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_FINAL_INSPECT (10/20/30 min) + TSK_STRL_FINAL_INSPECT (15/30/45 min). Combined: QT3: 20 min (scan all components). QT4: 35 min (systematic review all components + junctions). QT5: 50 min (critical inspection, zero tolerance). Not fully additive — inspect as single integrated system.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Defects Found During Final Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TOUCHUP (5/15/20 min) + TSK_STRL_TOUCHUP (10/20/30 min). Combined: QT3: 10 min. QT4: 25 min. QT5: 35 min. Correct all defects across all components. Feather into surrounding finish.

task_production_rates.name: Feel Test on Handrails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_FEEL_TEST_HANDRAIL (120 LF/hr). ~30 sec/LF. Run hand along handrail — must feel glass-smooth. QT5 only. In RP, existing surface may have prior paint nibs making this test even more important.

task_production_rates.name: Apply Polyurethane Topcoat on Handrails
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_POLY_TOPCOAT_HANDRAIL (50 LF/hr). Optional QT5. Single coat water-based poly. Thin, even application. Allow enamel to fully cure first (24-48 hours). Handrails only — not balusters, newels, or risers.

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall Handrail Brackets
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_BRACKET_REINSTALL (10 EA/hr). ~6 min/bracket. Reinstall from labeled bags, align to marks, secure, touch-up. QT4+ only.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Spray Containment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRL_REMOVE_SPRAY_CONTAIN (20 min FIXED). Remove cardboard shields, Tape & Drape. Spray method only.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Wall Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_REMOVE_WALL_MASK / TSK_STRL_REMOVE_WALL_MASK (both 200 LF/hr). Score tape edge, pull at 45-degree angle.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Carpet Runner Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Remove rosin paper and low-tack tape from carpet runner. Verify no paint transfer. ~15 min per system. Teardown is faster than setup (20 min) — no precision tape placement needed.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Floor Protection at Landings
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_REMOVE_FLOOR_PROTECT / TSK_STRL_REMOVE_FLOOR_PROTECT (both 300 SF/hr). Fold and remove canvas drops.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Tread Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: DIRECT transfer from TSK_STRS_REMOVE_TREAD_PROTECT / TSK_STRL_REMOVE_TREAD_PROTECT (both 40 EA/hr). ~1.5 min per tread. Score tape edges, remove Ram Board carefully. LAST task — may defer if tread work follows.

task_production_rates.name: Customer Walkthrough — Stairway System Review
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: RP_NEW task. Post-completion review with homeowner. Walk entire stairway, verify all components painted consistently, handrail smooth to touch, treads safe. ~12 min per stairway system (midpoint of 10-15 min per research RF-017). No NC equivalent.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools and Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Consolidated from TSK_STRS_TOOL_CLEANUP (20 min) + TSK_STRL_TOOL_CLEANUP (25 min). Combined RP spec: single tool cleanup session. ~25 min. Includes German round brushes, angled sash brushes, spray equipment (if used). Not additive — same cleanup station.

quality_tier_effects.source: Modifier_Registry.md v1.2 — global QT modifiers for stairs (no surface-specific override)
quality_tier_effects.applies_to: qt_scaled tasks only (assessment, degloss, scrape/feather, caulk assess, interstage inspect/sand/patch/spot coat, spot prime, final inspect, touchup)
quality_tier_effects.does_not_apply_to: binary tasks — application rates (brush/spray finish, prime), protection setup/teardown, assessment adhesion/coating_id/antislip, fixed overhead tasks
quality_tier_effects.notes: Stairs use GLOBAL QT modifiers (1.0/1.3/1.5), not surface-specific overrides. QT2 is excluded — stairs are scrutinized, prominent surfaces per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1. QT3 is minimum.

round_configurations.description: 2 finish coats only — no prime needed

estimation_notes.dual_uom: Six paintable items with dual UOM: risers (EA), balusters (EA), newels (EA), stringers (LF), handrails (LF), base rails (LF). Total labor = riser_hours + stringer_hours + baluster_hours + newel_hours + handrail_hours + base_rail_hours + fixed_hours. Most complex multi-UOM calculation in the RP portfolio.
estimation_notes.baluster_count_driver: Baluster count is the DOMINANT cost driver (same as NC). A system with 62 turned balusters at 7 min/EA x 3 coats = ~22 hours of baluster painting alone. Always validate baluster count input.
estimation_notes.access_staging_overhead: Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 5.6: 15-40% of total stairway project time consumed by access staging. This is a project-level overhead — not modeled per-task. Factor into overall project estimate.
estimation_notes.spray_vs_brush_tradeoff: Spray is 2.5-3x faster for application but requires 45+ min containment setup (spray_contain). Break-even at ~20-25 balusters. In RP occupied context, brush is even more dominant due to containment difficulty in inhabited stairwells.
estimation_notes.consolidation_savings: Combined RP spec eliminates duplicate setup/teardown, interstage, and cleanup from NC riser + railing specs. Consolidated tasks are NOT fully additive — single-pass efficiency reduces combined times.
estimation_notes.no_dry_times: Per RC-004: no dry times specified. Refer to manufacturer PDS.
estimation_notes.task_count_verification: 69 total tasks: 7 setup + 4 assessment + 5 RRP + 14 prep + 8 prime + 7 interstage + 12 finish + 12 cleanup = 69. sop_modules.json task_count_summary corrected from 68 to 69 during QA. All 69 tasks have matching production rates.
